articles.title: US moves to restrict birthright citizenship for children of foreign government employees: All you need to know
articles.summary: US News: The US Department of Homeland Security has introduced a new rule affecting birthright citizenship for children born to foreign government employees. This change expands citizenship exceptions and highlights the legal implications for future offspring of certain foreign nationals.
articles.body: Children born in the US to certain foreign government employees could be denied automatic citizenship under a new rule issued by the Department of Homeland Security, widening an exception that has traditionally covered children of foreign diplomats.The interim final rule, issued on September 4, applies when neither parent is a US citizen and at least one parent is a qualifying foreign government employee at the time of the child’s birth.What has changed under the new rule?Federal regulations previously referred specifically to children born to foreign diplomatic officers. DHS has replaced that wording with the broader term “foreign government employee”, extending the category to additional workers connected to foreign governments and international organisations.The change does not automatically affect every child of a foreign national working in the US. It applies only when the parent meets the rule’s definition and neither parent is a US citizen.Who could be covered?The definition includes accredited foreign diplomatic officers, certain embassy and consulate employees who are nationals of the country they represent, people employed by a foreign government in an official capacity and employees of international organisations that have immunity in the US.The parent must hold the relevant position when the child is born for the exception to apply.Who is excluded?The rule does not cover personal employees of foreign officials, including workers such as chauffeurs and housekeepers. It also excludes certain employees of state-owned enterprises, third-country nationals working for foreign governments and contractors who do not fall within the specified categories.Foreign government employees visiting the US for personal reasons are also outside the definition.What status can affected children seek?Children covered by the rule can voluntarily apply for lawful permanent residence through Form I-485. If the application is approved, their permanent resident status will be treated as beginning on the date of birth.DHS is also revising Form G-325R for children who do not acquire US citizenship at birth and do not choose to register as permanent residents. Those children may still be required to comply with federal alien-registration requirements.How does the rule relate to birthright citizenship?The Fourteenth Amendment generally grants citizenship to people born in the US who are subject to its jurisdiction. US law has long recognised limited exceptions, including children of foreign diplomatic representatives.DHS says the new rule expands the regulatory framework for that exception by replacing the narrower diplomatic-officer category with the broader foreign-government-employee classification.Is the rule being enforced?The rule applies prospectively to children born on or after its effective date. Children born before that date are not subject to the new requirements.Its implementation is also limited by ongoing litigation. In Casa Inc. v. Trump, a federal judge in Maryland issued a preliminary injunction on September 2 blocking enforcement of the administration’s birthright citizenship restrictions against members of the certified class covered by the case.DHS said it will not apply the rule to those individuals, or take action that conflicts with the injunction, unless the government obtains relief from the court.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Russian ambassador: Leipzig incident may have ended "very differently"
articles.summary: Russia's ambassador to Germany, Sergei Nechayev, in a new interview, has rejected claims that his country was behind last month's botched bomb attack at Leip...
articles.body:
Ukrainian Antonov aircraft parked at Leipzig/Halle Airport following the drone incident on August 5, 2026, where a drone equipped for an attack was seized near a Ukrainian transport aircraft.

Russia's ambassador to Germany, Sergei Nechayev, rejected claims that his country was behind the botched bomb attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport, stating no evidence has been produced to support the accusation.

Berlin believes Russian intelligence services are behind the discovery of drones carrying explosives at the eastern airport, leading to reciprocal shutdowns of cultural institutions between Russia and Germany.

Russia's ambassador to Germany, Sergei Nechayev, in a new interview, has rejected claims that his country was behind last month's botched bomb attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport - an incident that has since resulted in the reciprocal shutdown of cultural institutions in both countries.

No evidence has been produced to support the accusation, Nechayev said during an interview on the popular Ben Berndt podcast Unscripted, which aired on Saturday.

"If we had really wanted to cause trouble in Leipzig, it could, as you certainly know, have looked very different," he said.

"But we have absolutely no intention of provoking the [German] population or the government," Nechayev stressed.

Berlin believes Russian intelligence services are behind the discovery of drones carrying explosives at the eastern airport. There were no consequences on site because an explosive device near a Ukrainian aircraft failed to detonate.

As a punitive measure, Russia must close its consulate general in Bonn and the Russian House cultural institute in Berlin. In response, Moscow has banned the German Goethe Institute representations across Russia.

"We don't want a war with NATO, we don't want a war against Germany," the ambassador said regarding the state of relations.

At the same time, he saw his country in conflict with NATO because its members, including Germany, supported Ukraine. This, he argued, made the NATO countries belligerent.

"We are fighting against NATO in the current situation," Nechayev said.

Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and has been trying unsuccessfully to subjugate its much smaller neighbour ever since.

articles.title: Watch: US strikes 3 Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets 2 navy warships
articles.summary: International News: US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers after Iran launched ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships, according to the US military. The strikes c.
articles.body: US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers after Iran launched ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships, according to the US military. The strikes came after the American vessels evaded multiple Iranian missile attacks, with the US military later releasing footage of the operation.According to US central command (CENTCOM), Iran launched ballistic missiles at two US navy warships, an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. The ships evaded multiple attacks, and no US personnel were injured in the incident.CENTCOM said the three tankers were part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that helps fund Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and its regional proxies.The US military said the M/T Downy was struck off Kharg Island and permanently disabled. The M/T Stark 1 was also permanently disabled near Jask. The third tanker, M/T Kylo, also known as Noxen, was struck in the Gulf of Oman and completely destroyed after its crew was directed to abandon the vessel.CENTCOM released video of the strikes, showing US forces targeting the Iranian oil tankers.US central command commander Admiral Brad Cooper said the strikes were intended to impose an economic cost on Iran after the missile attacks on US navy ships.“If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost, taking out three of yours,” Cooper said.The US military said Iran had no effective means to defend the tankers during the operation.The strikes add another dimension to the ongoing US-Iran confrontation, with the US targeting vessels it says are connected to Iran’s oil trade and the financing of the IRGC.

articles.title: At least 22 killed in fire at wedding party in Congo’s Kinshasa
articles.summary: Rest of World News: At least 22 people were killed in a fire at a wedding party in Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, the mayor of the city’s Ling.
articles.body: At least 22 people were killed in a fire at a wedding party in Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, the mayor of the city’s Lingwala district said on Saturday.The fire broke out overnight Friday and continued into the early hours of Saturday in a building in Lingwala, in northern Kinshasa. Several other people were injured.The mayor of Lingwala, Norbert Mushinga, told the Congolese Press Agency that the provisional death toll was 22 and warned that it could rise further.Victims carried out as people fledAs the fire spread, people attending the wedding tried to help those trapped inside. Several victims, both alive and dead, were laid along the roadside as people attempted to assist the injured.The narrow hallways of the building became congested as people tried to escape the fire.The exact cause of the blaze has not yet been confirmed.“It is a tragedy,” Congo’s deputy Prime Minister and interior minister Jacquemin Shabani said after visiting the site on Saturday morning.Kinshasa sees frequent deadly firesDeadly fires are common in densely populated parts of Kinshasa, where urban development has not been accompanied by adequate provisions such as fire services.Such fires are particularly common during the dry season, with several reported in Kinshasa this year, according to local media.Authorities have yet to confirm what caused the wedding-party fire or provide a final toll.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
